newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - New Hanson's first post-demerger H1.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - New Hanson's first post-demerger H1.

text.p: The new Hanson Plc, the rump building group left over from the former conglomerate's four-way demerger, reports its debut set of first-half results next Thursday.
Analysts said there was no comparable benchmark for first-half, pre-tax profits. Some said they would therefore be looking for the operating profit figure on a continuing business basis.
The first half will cover the normal two-quarter period, with the second half spanning three quarters due to Hanson changing its financial year to match the calender year following the demerger.
Kevin Cammack, analyst at Merrill Lynch, said he would be looking for the first-half operating profit figure of 76 million versus 65 million for an on-going business basis.
He warned the pre-tax profit figure would be distorted by exceptionals due to the demerger itself.
The period is seen including the U.S. Concrete Pipe acquisition for 78 million stg in March.
But it is not expected to cover the recent sale of the Hanson Electrical unit to a management group for at least 135 million stg. That is seen incurring a provision for the third quarter.
The underlying trading result is expected to show a better performance in the UK which has seen buoyant commercial and private housing sectors.
But other sluggish European markets are not expected to hurt Hanson as they have other building players because of Hanson's relatively small exposure to continental Europe.
The U.S. is seen remaining firm, said Merrill Lynch.
The dividend payout for the period is expected to be four pence per share.
